COURT’S OR JUDGES’S ORDERS
BA1 No.483 of 2026
Hon’ble Pankaj Purohit, J.
Ms. Sheetal Selwal, learned counsel for the 
applicant.
2. Mr. Vijay Khanduri, learned Brief Holder for the 
State.
3. Applicant is under incarceration in connection with 
FIR No.89 of 2026, registered under Section 8/21 of the 
Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, 1985, 
at Police Station Kichha, District Udham Singh Nagar, 
since 09.03.2026.
4. Applicant has moved a short-term bail application 
(IA No.2 of 2026) seeking his release for the purpose of 
appearing in the B.Com. 2nd Semester Examination, 
scheduled to be conducted from 10.06.2026 to 
03.07.2026. In the said application, applicant has 
submitted that he has already passed the B.Com. 1st
Semester Examination and now wants to appear in the 
B.Com. 2nd Semester Examination. The admit card for 
the 2nd Semester Examination has been annexed as 
Annexure-SA1 to the supplementary affidavit. In 
paragraph 3 of the supplementary affidavit, it has been 
stated that applicant's examinations are scheduled to be 
held on 10.06.2026, 12.06.2026, 16.06.2026, and 
03.07.2026. Accordingly, applicant has prayed for his 
release on short-term bail. 
5. Learned counsel appearing for the State submits 
that it is correct that the applicant has to appear in the  2
B.Com. 2nd Semester Examination. 
6. In view of the aforesaid facts and circumstances, the 
short-term bail application is allowed. 
7. The applicant-Mohd. Shahwaz, is directed to be 
released on short-term bail with effect from 09.06.2026 
till 03.07.2026, subject to his executing a personal bond 
and furnishing two reliable sureties of the like amount 
each to the satisfaction of the concerned Special Judge, 
NDPS. Applicant shall surrender before the concerned 
Special Judge, NDPS on 04.07.2026. 
8. Applicant shall utilize the period of short-term bail 
solely for the purpose for which it has been granted and 
shall maintain good conduct throughout the said period.
9. List on 14.07.2026.
10. Let certified copy of this order be issued to the 
learned counsel for the applicant today itself on payment 
of usual charges.
(Pankaj Purohit, J.)
09.06.2026 AK

Ms. Sheetal Selwal, learned counsel for the applicant.
2. Mr. Chitrarth Kandpal, learned Brief Holder for the 
State.
3. Today, the matter is listed on time extension application 
(IA No.3/2026). 
4. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that time 
extension application has rendered infructuous for the 
reason that petitioner has already surrendered before the jail 
authority and he is now under incarceration. 
5. Accordingly, time extension application is dismissed as 
infructuous. 
6. Learned counsel for the State submits that State has 
filed its objections along with delay condonation application 
(IA No.1/2026). For the reasons stated, delay condonation 
application is allowed. Delay in filing the objections is 
condoned. Objections filed on behalf of the State are taken on 
record.
7. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that she does 
not wish to file any reply to the objections filed by the State.
8. List on 03.08.2026.
(Pankaj Purohit, J.)
14.07.2026 AK

Ms. Nashra, learned counsel holding brief of 
Ms. Sheetal Selwal, learned counsel for the 
applicant.
2. Mr. Vipul Painuly, learned AGA along with Mr. 
Chitrarth Kandpal, learned Brief Holder for the State.
3. Today, the matter is listed on the second short￾term bail application (IA No.4/2026). By means of the 
said short-term bail application, applicant seeks his 
release on short-term bail on account of suffering 
from jaundice.
4. The attention of this Court has been drawn by 
the learned State Counsel to page 17 of the second 
short-term bail application, wherein the doctor has 
opined that applicant is to have rest for a period of 
one month from 26.06.2026. Learned State Counsel 
submits that the said period has already expired, as 
the applicant has already undergone the said period 
inside the jail, during which he had been advised to 
take rest. Thus, according to him, no case is made 
out for releasing the applicant on short-term bail.
5. Having heard the learned counsel for the parties  and upon perusal of the record, this Court is of the 
opinion that no good ground is made out to release 
the applicant on short-term bail. Accordingly, the 
second short-term bail application (IA No.4/2026) is 
hereby rejected.
6. List on 24.08.2026.
(Pankaj Purohit, J.)
03.08.2026 AK
